label: The <!-- skill_agent: X --> owner marker carried by 17 of 44 shipped command files is absent from sk-doc's prescribed command frontmatter (description, argument-hint, allowed-tools) and is read by no code: a repo-wide grep of .cjs/.mjs/.ts/.py/.json/.yaml outside deep-review returns zero hits, so the tag documents a consumer that does not exist while duplicating skillId/ownerMode already held in command-metadata.json. The unrelated deep-review overlay of the same name makes a searcher believe it is wired.

/doctor:ci grants Write in allowed-tools while its own router contract forbids editing workflow YAML and its scaffold step writes through ci-scaffold.cjs under the Bash grant; Write appears exactly once in the file, at the frontmatter line. Removing it breaks nothing because the script owns the write.

REPO RULES.md section 4 calls Delivery one of two rules whose trigger is a whole turn, the other being handback, but the trigger table has four whole-turn rows (Write any substantive reply; Draft or edit any sentence; Present a recommendation; End a turn), counted at 4. A maintainer deciding where a new rule belongs reads an undercount that makes a fifth turn-scoped rule look like a category error.

All 13 rule files ship title/description/trigger_phrases/importance_tier/contextType/version, but the committed trigger index holds zero repo-rules/<file>.md paths, so no runtime reads those phrases and Gate 1 (every turn) can never surface a rule file: only Gate 5 on a write can. Removing the frontmatter breaks nothing measurable today; indexing the 13 files would close the hole AGENTS.md section 4 patches by hand.

REPO RULES.md rule 4 says the more specific trigger wins on conflict, but the precedence table ranks every rule file identically at level 3, no rule file declares a specificity rank, and importance_tier is important-or-normal on nearly all of them, which is not an ordering. The clause is unexecutable, so an agent invents a ranking at the one moment it should not be improvised.

v4.0.0.1 bumped blast-radius.md from version 1.0.1.0 to 1.0.1.2, skipping 1.0.1.1 with no intermediate commit, in a field no reader consumes and no changelog compares: HEAD now reads 1.0.1.4 there and 1.1.1.5 in evidence-and-proof.md, five hand bumps across this release line. The manual counter cannot detect its own skip.

The rule directory is fully reachable and uniform: .skilled/repo-rules/ holds 13 files, REPO RULES.md's trigger table holds 13 rows, one per file, with no orphan file and no dangling row; AGENTS.md names 8 of the 13 in prose; every section anchor the two router documents cite resolves (communication-handoff 1 and 5, uncertainty-and-honesty 7, prevent-overengineering 2, scope-discipline 5 and 6); all 13 files carry the same six frontmatter keys in the same order.

Negative result recorded deliberately: the iteration set out to find repo-rules frontmatter outliers and orphaned rule files and found none, so the six findings are the residue after that hypothesis failed, not the most available thing to report.

sk-doc's argument-hint budget of 140 characters is honoured by the doctor routers examined: ci.md is 45 characters and runtime-mirrors.md is 16, so the command-format departures are about identity metadata and tool grants rather than invocation shape.

direction: Repo-rules frontmatter outliers and orphaned rule files (AGENTS.md versus REPO RULES.md reachability mismatch)
reason: All 13 files exist, all 13 have a trigger-table row, all 13 share the same six-key frontmatter shape, and every cited section anchor resolves. The mismatch hypothesis is dead; the surviving defects are internal to REPO RULES.md (undercounted whole-turn rules, unexecutable specificity clause) and to the rule frontmatter having no consumer.
